extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, industry stakeholders, regulated entities, small businesses, and others interested in CFPB rulemaking and commenting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau develops rules, seeks public input, and handles petitions, advisory committees, and small-business review for rulemakings. Useful for potential commenters, regulated firms, and other stakeholders engaging with CFPB rule processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking starts with research and public input
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB’s rulemaking process typically starts with research and is further informed by public input, including field hearings, consumer and industry roundtables, advisory bodies, and in some cases, small business review panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific forms of input (field hearings, roundtables, advisory bodies, small business review panels) as part of the evidence base for rulemaking; implies these are valid avenues for stakeholders to influence rule development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess benefits and costs of regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: We carefully assess the benefits and costs of the regulations we are considering for consumers and financial institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of proposed rules should include consideration of impacts on consumers and on financial institutions; cost-benefit assessment is a stated part of CFPB's process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish proposed rules to solicit public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rules are generally published to give industry, consumers, and other external stakeholders an opportunity to comment on their potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publication of proposed rules creates a formal notice-and-comment opportunity; stakeholders should comment during that period to influence final outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide support and resources after rule finalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a regulation is in place, we provide support and resources to help stakeholders understand and comply with the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB commits to post-rule assistance (guidance, tools, explanatory resources) to facilitate compliance and understanding by regulated parties and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Interactive Bureau Regulations to make regulations accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactive Bureau Regulations makes regulations easier to read and navigate by bringing related information and regulatory history together with the rule text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tool is a work in progress and may not yet contain all regulations; intended to improve accessibility and contextual understanding of rules and their histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage Small Business Review Panel for significant economic impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn about how the CFPB works with the Small Business Review Panel on rules that could have significant economic impacts on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For rules with potentially significant economic impact on small entities, CFPB involvement with the Small Business Review Panel is part of the process—this is a procedural safeguard and consultation mechanism for small business concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish notices requesting public comment on varied documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB publishes notices requesting public comment on a variety of documents, including proposed rules and requests for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone may comment—'You don’t have to be an expert or a lawyer to give comments. We invite everyone to share their views.' This frames comments as open to all stakeholders, not just experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to petitions for rulemaking as required by the APA
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB responds to petitions from interested persons for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a CFPB rule, as required by the Administrative Procedure Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners can request rule issuance, amendment, or repeal; CFPB response obligations are governed by APA procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convene advisory committees for formal input
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB convenes four independent groups for formal input on everything from consumer engagement, to policy development, to research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory committees are a formal channel for structured stakeholder input across multiple topic areas; they inform policy, engagement strategies, and research priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider special impacts on community banks and credit unions
rubrics_metrics.description: We work with community banks and credit unions to ensure consumers can choose among a variety of products, services, and financial relationships. We especially consider how our rules affect community banks and credit unions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB highlights attention to how rules affect smaller depository institutions—this signals targeted consideration of compliance burden and market effects on these entities during rule development.
